findings.quote:
inline fun <reified T> ReflectionHints.getTypeHint() =
	getTypeHint(T::class.java)

inline fun <reified T> ReflectionHints.registerType(noinline typeHint: (TypeHint.Builder) -> Unit) =
	registerType(T::class.java, typeHint::invoke)

inline fun <reified T> ReflectionHints.registerType(vararg memberCategories: MemberCategory) =
	registerType(T::class.java, *memberCategories)
findings.explanation: All three extensions materialize the reified Kotlin type as T::class.java. Lookup delegates to Java getTypeHint(Class<?>). Builder customization delegates to registerType(Class<?>, Consumer), adapting the non-inlined Kotlin function through typeHint::invoke, so Java controls whether and when it runs. The category extension spreads the Kotlin vararg into Java registerType(Class<?>, MemberCategory...), forwarding every supplied element.

Both Class-based registration overloads first reject a null Class with IllegalArgumentException. A non-null Class lacking a canonical name is instead silently skipped and the method returns this. Because delegation is inside the canonical-name condition, a supplied customizer is not called for either a rejected null Class or a skipped no-canonical-name Class; likewise, skipped category registration applies no categories.

Registration stores or retrieves one builder per equal TypeReference, then applies each customizer to that same builder. Category registration becomes a builder customizer; withMembers adds categories to a HashSet, so repeated registrations form a deduplicated set union. There is no rollback or exception handling around accept: a thrown exception propagates, but the builder was already inserted. Existing categories and categories added before the throw remain. For a newly inserted type whose customizer throws before adding a category, the type remains registered with an empty category set.

For a valid Class, lookup first converts it to a TypeReference and reads the map; an unregistered valid type returns null, whereas registration creates a builder and therefore an entry. Unlike Class-based registration, lookup does not pre-skip a Class with no canonical name: TypeReference.of delegates to ReflectionTypeReference.of, which throws IllegalArgumentException when getCanonicalName() is null. That factory also rejects a null Class with "'type' must not be null"; registration performs its own equivalent null assertion before delegation.

Each lookup builds a TypeHint whose category set is an immutable copy of the builder's categories. Consequently, a previously returned TypeHint and its returned category set do not change when the same type is registered again. A later lookup builds a new TypeHint that observes the builder's newly accumulated category set.
